title: Six Rules for Resizable Panels
summary: This lesson covers essential UX improvements for resizable split views, focusing on interaction robustness and state persistence. It details technical solutions for common issues like small hit areas, iframe interference, and cursor flickering.

transcript.text: This layout looks fine until you drag the divider off the screen.
The visible divider is one pixel. The grab target has to be 12.
Miss it and the resize feels stuck.
Clamp every drag between a min and a max width so a panel can never collapse into something you cannot reopen.
Near the edge, snap it fully closed instead of leaving a sliver.
Halfway states read like bugs. Commit to open or shut.
While dragging, drop an invisible overlay over the whole page.
Otherwise an iframe or a text selection eats the mouse and the panel freezes mid-drag.
Set the resize cursor on the whole body, not the handle alone.
The arrow shouldn't flicker when you drift a pixel off. Keep it locked.
Remember the width across reloads or you throw away the exact layout the user set by hand.
Go to designmotionhq.com for more. Link in bio.

on_screen_text: HIT AREA Grow the grab zone.
SNAP Commit to open or shut.
Lock the cursor on the body.
design_principles: Increase hit area for small targets
before_after: A fragile split view that can be dragged off-screen or lose focus is transformed into a robust, constrained, and persistent resizable panel system.
